newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury says Mexico should push reforms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury says Mexico should push reforms.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury, in a semi-annual report to Congress, said its monitoring of the Mexican economy following its financial rescue package has underscored the position that economic reforms should be pressed.

The monitoring and consultations have "underscored the position that Mexico should maintain sound fiscal and monetary policies, improve transparency and dissemination of economic and financial data, (and) push forward structural reforms," the report said.
In addition, the department said its discussions have made clear that the country should rebuild reserves and repay the U.S. support package through financings in the international capital markets.
The report said the country has "made substantial progress" in solidifying the independence of the Bank of Mexico, conducting strict monetary policy and stabilizing the peso.
"As an independent central bank, the Bank of Mexico has clearly stated its monetary policy goals and has enacted policies designed to achieve them," the report said.

The report also said that Mexico continued to satisfy its commitments under the financial agreements signed in February of 1995, adding that the goverment has adopted a rigorous adjustment program to put its economy on a path of sustained growth.
As of Dec 20, $13.5 billion in U.S. funds have been disbursed to Mexico under the support program. Of this amount, $3.5 billion in medium term swaps remain outstanding.
